highlight.title: The Temporal Dynamics of Team Psychological Safety: A Perishable Resource
highlight.summary: New research reveals that psychological safety in teams isn't static but can diminish as well as grow over time, shaped by four key processes: connecting, clarifying, supporting, and performing. Time alone doesn't build safety—teams must actively sustain these processes.

resources.title: A Framework for Accelerated Leadership Development in the Workplace
resources.why_now: This 2024 research addresses the gap between leadership program inputs and outcomes by considering learning processes and learner preferences. Essential for leaders designing development programs that actually stick.

resources.title: Psychological Safety in Interdisciplinary Teams: How Leadership Behaviors Empower
resources.why_now: Fresh insights on how leaders can cultivate awareness of power dynamics and make implicit team norms explicit. Practical for managers working with diverse, cross-functional teams where status differences can silence voices.

resources.title: Understanding Decision Making in Organizational Contexts: A Framework for Effective Choices
resources.why_now: Combines psychology, economics, and management theory to examine cognitive biases and emotional influences in organizational decision-making. Timely as leaders navigate complex choices amid uncertainty and competing stakeholder demands.

resources.title: 2024 Global Leadership Development Study: Time to Transform
resources.why_now: Based on 1,100+ L&D professionals, reveals that 70% believe leaders need to master wider behavioral ranges for transformation efforts. Critical for understanding current leadership capability gaps in rapidly changing organizations.

claude_take: The research consistently shows that traditional leadership approaches—fixed styles, time-based team building, rational decision models—are insufficient for today's complex organizational realities. The most compelling insight is that psychological safety is perishable and requires active cultivation through specific behaviors, not just good intentions or team retreats.
